### 1. What the user expresses, and how the simulator behaves

The caller states the target object and the mode of authorisation plainly, and nothing else:

> "she wants to clear what the demand service account owes today and be done with it, and she
> would rather pay it on the company card there and then"

> "She is content for the desk to make whatever postings it has to make on its own side, and says
> as much if the agent tells her there is something to put right on the account first; but the card
> is hers, so she will not have anyone else run the payment for her, and she will do that part
> herself once she is told the figure and handed the means to do it."

- **Target object**: what the demand service account owes — the rate program at account level.
- **Timing**: today, at the frozen moment.
- **Boundary**: she authorises the desk's own postings in advance but reserves the payment act.
- **Authorisation mode**: the payment is an owner act, handed over and run by the user.

The simulator is passive throughout. It conveys the need, answers what it is asked
("she reads out the account number 620147 … the last four of the company's federal tax number,
2214"), volunteers the September RTU-3 call **only if the agent raises it first**, and will not
guess at any figure ("She does not know what the invoices add up to and will not guess at it").
It executes one user tool when handed over ("Once the agent hands the payment over for her to run
herself, she says I'll put it on the company card while I've got you and runs it"). It never
pushes the procedure along: "Until she is either given the figure or handed the payment she stays
where she is". There is no leak of any figure and no hint of the next step.

**Act now.** Every ground is visible and satisfied:

  least two of them match". The caller supplies exactly those two.
- The account exists and is active: `find_customers` → `account_status: 'active'`,
  `credit_terms: 'net_30'`, customer_id `05004549-2fb8-48f5-8057-744e16f5d00f`.
- One program stands: `find_service_programs` → `variant_name: 'Block Hour Service Program'`,
  `status: 'active'`, `term_start_date: '2026-02-01'`, `term_end_date: '2027-01-31'`,
  `credit_limit_usd: 25000.0`, `po_required: 'false'`, `last_change_type: 'credit_limit_changed'`,
  `last_change_date: '2026-02-01'`.
- The request is squarely covered: *Demand Service Rate Programs: Payment Clearing What Is Owed on
  a Demand Service Account* — "An owner holding a rate program under the Demand Service Rate
  Programs may ask to settle the demand service account, paying money off the account so that what
  is owed on it is cleared." Nothing here is POLICY_NOT_COVERED, and she never asks for a person.

**(a) Labor line for WO-4471902.** *Working Out the Labor Line of a Completed Call* is the
computation document; the call it names is "the call last completed on the rate program", i.e.
WO-4471902 (completed 2026-09-12).

- *Hours charged for.* The baseline takes logged hours rounded up to the next quarter hour (2.6 →
  2.75). But the record carries `hours_band: 'after_hours'`, and *Minimum Hours Standing on a
  Dispatched Call* rules: "Where the call record puts the hours outside regular hours and the hours
  logged fall short of the tier's after-hours minimum, the after-hours minimum stands as the hours
  charged for." The tier's after-hours minimum is 3.0 and 2.6 falls short → **3.0 hours**.
- *Hours billed.* The baseline bills every hour charged for. *Prepaid Hours Standing Against the
  Hours of a Call*, Term A, applies because the tier's rollover column is Yes and blocks stand
  bought within the 12-month expiry period: hours of every block bought within that period
  (2025-11-20 and 2026-03-05: 40 + 40 = **80**; the 2025-08-14 block expired 2026-08-14) less the
  hours drawn by the calls completed in the same period ahead of it (14.0 + 22.5 + 16.0 + 9.0 +
  17.0 = **78.5**) = **1.5** prepaid hours available; "only the hours of the call beyond that
  balance are billed" → 3.0 − 1.5 = **1.5 hours billed**.
- *Rate.* The baseline is the block overage rate 144. *Labor Rate on a Call at a Building Under a
  Maintenance Agreement*, Second: the account holds an active agreement at a tier that does not
  cover repair labor (Preventive Maintenance Agreement — the maintenance repair-coverage table has
  "no" in its repair-labor column), the call was worked at Northgate Commons which is the building
  that agreement runs at, the program's substitution column is Yes, and the agreement's published
  labor rate 136 is lower than the block overage rate 144 → **rate 136**.
- *Premium.* The baseline is 1.0. *Premiums Carried by the Hour Band of a Call*: hours the record
  puts outside regular hours carry the after-hours multiplier → **1.5**.
- *Further technicians.* The baseline bills nothing. *What a Second Technician on a Call Is Billed
  At*: "more than one technician on a call taken at emergency or critical priority" → the second
  journeyman rate for the hours charged for. `technician_count: 2`, priority emergency → 1 beyond
  the lead at 138.
- Assembly per the computation document: hours billed × rate × premium, plus (technicians beyond
  the lead × hours charged for × that technician's rate × the same premium), total rounded half up:
  1.5 × 136 × 1.5 = 306.00; 1 × 3.0 × 138 × 1.5 = 621.00; **labor line = 927.00**.

**(b) Missed response credit for WO-4471902.** *Working Out the Credit for a Missed Response*.

- *Labor element.* Baseline: logged hours at the block hour rate. *The Labor Element Behind a
  Response Credit*: "Where a demand service charge line of the labor kind stands on the rate
  program for the call the credit arises from, the labor element is that line." Once (a) is booked
  such a line stands → **927.00**.
- *Attendance element.* Baseline: the tier's trip charge 85. *The Attendance Element Where a
  Maintenance Agreement Is Held*, Judgement 2: the active agreement's published trip charge (65) is
  lower than the program's own (85) → **65**.
- *Credit rate.* Baseline 25 percent. *Severity of a Missed Response and the Credit Rate*: the call
  was accepted at emergency priority and the technician reached the building on a later calendar
  day (accepted 2026-09-11 19:05, onsite 2026-09-12 14:20) → the tier's credit rate taken at 1.5 →
  **37.5 percent**.
- *Uplift.* Baseline 1.0. *Uplift Where Responses Have Been Missed Before*: calls completed on the
  program in the current program year (term start 2026-02-01 → today) carrying the response
  recorded as missed: WO-4471204, WO-4471741, WO-4471902 = **three or more → 1.25**. WO-4470663
  (2026-01-15) falls before the current term start and is not counted.
- Assembly: (927.00 + 65) × 37.5 per hundred × 1.25 = 992.00 × 0.375 = 372.00; × 1.25 = 465.00;
  rounded 465.00; below the ceiling of 750 → **credit = 465.00**.

**(c) The billing month's late fee.** *Working Out the Month's Arrears Late Fee*. Window = the 12
months to the day the fee is raised, i.e. 2025-09-17 → 2026-09-17.

- *Invoiced total in the window* (charges with a due day in it): 5280.00 + 5280.00 + 1300.00 +
  1842.50 = **13702.50** (INV-40881207, due 2025-09-13, falls outside).
- *Amount the fee runs on.* Baseline: the whole invoiced total. *Payments Standing Against the
  Invoiced Total of an Arrears Fee*: payments received in the window are 5280.00 + 5280.00 +
  900.00 = 11460.00, above nil and below the invoiced total → "the invoiced total less those
  payments" = **2242.50**.
- *Monthly rate.* Baseline: 1.5 percent, no step. *Stepped Monthly Rates on Demand Service
  Arrears*: the most recent invoice to fall due is INV-41051182 (due 2026-08-15), 33 days past due
  — not longer than the suspension period of 45, but longer than the payment term of 30 — and the
  open position (13702.50 − 11460.00 = 2242.50) is at or below the credit limit of 25000 →
  **1.75 percent**. *Step for the Owner's Other Accounts on an Arrears Fee*: an active Preventive
  Maintenance Agreement stands, and its installments falling due in the same window (4 × 3600.00 =
  14400.00) are cleared by the payments received on it in that window (4 × 3600.00 = 14400.00) →
  **0.25 percent taken off**. Monthly rate = 1.75 − 0.25 = **1.5 percent**.
- *Months charged.* Baseline 1. *The Run of Months an Arrears Fee Covers*: the most recent payment
  (2026-08-16) reached the office later than the day the most recent invoice fell due (2026-08-15)
  and the window's payments do not clear the invoiced total → the months run from 2026-08-16,
  counting each month or part month up to 2026-09-17 = one whole month plus a part month = **2**.
- *Handling charge.* Baseline nil. *Handling Charge on a Month's Arrears Fee*: four invoices fell
  due in the window (two or more), the payments leave part of the invoiced total standing, and the
  open position 2242.50 is at or below the credit limit → **40 US dollars**.
- Assembly: 2242.50 × 1.5 percent = 33.6375; × 2 months = 67.275; + 40 = 107.275; only the total
  rounded, half up → **late fee = 107.28**.

**(d) The figure that clears the account.** *Working Out the Figure That Clears a Demand Service
Account*. Ledger window = 24 months back from today (2024-09-17 →).

- *Charges taken in.* Baseline: only those fallen due within the window. *Which Charges a
  Settlement Takes In*, Judgement 1: once (a) and (c) are booked, charges stand that have not
  fallen due within the window — the hub says of both lines that they are "raised without a due
  day, and … dated for payment when the billing month's invoice is issued", and the settlement hub
  repeats "A charge line raised on the program during the billing month stands without a due day
  until the billing month's invoice is issued, and until then it has not fallen due" — while
  charges also stand that have fallen due within it → "every charge invoiced on the program is
  taken in, fallen due or not": 5280.00 + 5280.00 + 5280.00 + 1300.00 + 1842.50 + 927.00 + 107.28 =
  **20016.78**.
- *Payments.* "every payment received on the program, over its whole life and not over a window" =
  5280.00 + 5280.00 + 5280.00 + 900.00 = **16740.00**.
- *Credits set off.* Baseline nil. *Which Credits a Settlement Sets Off*: a credit stands issued in
  the current billing month (the 465.00 of (b)) and a charge stands that has not fallen due within
  the ledger window → "every credit standing on the program is set off" = **465.00**.
- *Emergency dispatch element.* Baseline nothing. *What the Program Year's Emergency Dispatches Add
  to a Settlement*: dispatches counted against the current program year (term start 2026-02-01 → today)
  are those of 2026-03-19, 2026-07-14 and 2026-09-11 = 3; the tier includes 2; 3 is above the
  included calls but not above twice them → the tier's surcharge of 250 for each of the 1 dispatch
  beyond → **250.00**.
- *Allowance.* Baseline nil. *The Allowance for Settling a Demand Service Account*: the most recent
  invoice fell due 2026-08-15, 33 days ago, no longer ago than the suspension period of 45, and
  payments stand received within the 24-month ledger window → **1.5 percent** on the charges taken
  in alone = 20016.78 × 0.015 = 300.2517.
- Assembly: 20016.78 − 16740.00 − 465.00 + 250.00 − 300.2517 = 2761.5283; only the total rounded,
  half up → **the figure that clears the account = 2761.53**.

Owners match the documents: the three postings say "The desk handles this itself"; the payment says

handed over, and the customer themselves runs it". `payment_method` is `credit_card` because she

or debit card charged on the spot". Terminal state: labor line, missed-response credit and late fee
standing on the program, and one payment entry of 2761.53 by credit_card clearing the account.

### 6. The problem tree derived from the visible materials alone

The customer asked for exactly one thing: settle the account. The tree:

```
settle the demand service account            (root — the customer's own write, user-owned)
├── the billing month's late fee line        (state-derived hop)
└── the labor charge for the call last completed
    └── the missed-response credit for that call   (state-derived hop, itself blocked by the labor charge)
```

Handling order: labor line → missed-response credit → late fee (order between the fee and the first
two is free) → payment.

**Hop 1 — root waits on the labor charge. state-derived.**
The blocked policy's own hub, *Payment Clearing What Is Owed on a Demand Service Account*, states:
> "The figure that clears the demand service account is settled only once the call last completed
> on the program carries its labor charge on the ledger."
The sentence names a **state** ("carries its labor charge on the ledger"), not an action. Query
`find_service_events` shows the call last completed is WO-4471902 (2026-09-12) and that the
program's `service_invoice_charged` rows carry `charge_type` `block_purchase`, `refrigerant` and
`parts` only — no labor charge on any work order, and none at all against WO-4471902. So the state
does not hold. Searching the corpus in the records' own words ("labor", "work order", "demand
service charge entry") reaches *Billing the Technician Labor of a Closed Demand Call*, which
describes the write that brings that state about: "A new demand service charge entry of the labor
kind is opened on the rate program, carrying the work order the labor was worked under, the money
amount billed for that labor". The chain is mine to draw: that document names no other problem and
the settlement hub names no tool of it.

**Hop 2 — root waits on the late fee line. state-derived.**
Same hub:
> "The figure that clears the demand service account is settled only after the late fee the billing
> month owes stands as a line on the rate program."
Again a state ("stands as a line on the rate program"). No `charge_type` on the program is a late
fee, so the state does not hold. The words "late fee" and "line … on the rate program" lead to
*The Billing Month's Late Fee on Demand Service Arrears*: "A single demand service charge entry of
the late fee kind is opened on the rate program, carrying the money amount of the fee and the
billing month it belongs to". That the fee is genuinely owed is separately visible: INV-41051182
fell due 2026-08-15 and 11460.00 of payments in the window stand against 13702.50 invoiced, so
demand service invoicing "has gone overdue" in that document's own words.

**Hop 3 — root waits on the missed-response credit. state-derived.**
Same hub:
> "The figure that clears the demand service account is settled only after the credit owed for the
> missed response on the call last completed on the program stands as a credit entry on the rate
> program."
A state again. No `service_credit_issued` row stands on the program. That the credit is owed at all
is derivable without the customer saying so: WO-4471902 carries `sla_met: 'missed'`, and
*When a Response Guarantee Is Missed* says "Where a technician reaches the building later than the
guarantee the call's classification carries, the customer is credited" — the call was accepted at
emergency priority at 2026-09-11 19:05 against an emergency commitment of 8 elapsed hours on this
tier, and the technician was on site 2026-09-12 14:20, some 19 hours later. None of the three
exclusions in that document applies (no access denial, no unreachable caller, no credit-limit
hold). The words "credit", "missed response", "credit entry on the rate program" reach
*Crediting the Owner for a Response Commitment Not Kept*, which describes the write: "One demand
service credit entry is opened on the rate program, marked as a missed response credit".

**Hop 4 — the credit waits on the labor charge. state-derived.**
*Crediting the Owner for a Response Commitment Not Kept* states in its own rule:
> "The credit for a missed response is worked out only once the labor charge for the call it arises
> from stands invoiced on the demand service account."
A state. It is unmet at the opening for the same reason as hop 1, and the same labor-line document
supplies the write. This edge is also what forces the order between the two agent postings, and it
is corroborated by the figure: *The Labor Element Behind a Response Credit* makes the labor element
"that line", so the credit cannot be computed before the line exists.

No hop was **pre-solved**: no prerequisite sentence names a tool, a policy id, a route or another
problem; no document strings the four problems into a procedure; each hop cost a records check and
a search on the state's own words.

### Two-way counter-proof

**The conclusion is fully supported.** Every figure above rests on a quoted sentence of the visible
corpus plus a row a finder returned; nothing needed a hidden field.

**Closest alternatives, each excluded by a visible sentence or record:**

| Alternative | What excludes it |
|---|---|
| The credit ceiling review / block purchase belongs here too | The settlement hub's three prerequisite sentences name only the labor charge, the late fee and the missed-response credit. No sentence anywhere makes a ceiling review or a block purchase a condition of settling, and the caller asks to pay, not to buy hours. |
| Use `block_hours_remaining: 18.5` from the program record as the prepaid balance | *Prepaid Hours Standing Against the Hours of a Call* defines the balance as computed — "the hours of every block bought within that period less the hours drawn by the calls completed in the same period ahead of it" — and the caller herself disclaims the stored figure ("whatever the portal shows is usually a fortnight behind"). Recorded as a policy-side note, not a document defect: the rule is definite, the stored field is not what the rule reads. |
| The call the credit arises from is WO-4471741 (also missed, also RTU-3, also emergency) | Both computation documents say "the call last completed on the rate program"; WO-4471902 completed 2026-09-12 is later than 2026-07-14. |
| The window for the arrears fee starts at the term start | *Working Out the Month's Arrears Late Fee* fixes it: "a due day falling in the 12 months to the day the fee is raised". |
| Payments over the life of the program reduce the fee | Same document: "neither do payments received outside that window". |
| The settlement takes in only charges that have fallen due | Excluded once the two new lines stand, by *Which Charges a Settlement Takes In* Judgement 1. Before they stand, the baseline would be right — which is exactly why the order matters. |
| `payment_method` `ach` or `check` | "she would rather pay it on the company card there and then than wait for the cheque run"; the tool enum defines `credit_card` as a company card charged on the spot. |
| The agent runs the payment for her | "the card is hers, so she will not have anyone else run the payment for her"; the hub: "This is the building owner's own act." |

**Against "do only the one thing the customer asked for".** Paying without the three postings is
excluded by reasoning, not by any route: the settlement hub's own rule makes the figure
underivable — "The figure that clears the demand service account is settled only once the call last
completed on the program carries its labor charge on the ledger", and likewise for the late fee
line and the credit entry. A payment taken before them leaves the governed result in a state the
visible principles forbid: the ledger would still owe an unbilled labor line and an unraised late
fee while an earned credit stood unissued, so "what is owed on it is cleared" (the hub's own
description of the request) would be false. Concretely the number moves: 2242.50 against 2761.53.

**The fall-back answers, computed from each computation document plus the product figures it names,
with no factor applied** (all definite, all different from the answers above):

| Computation | Fall-back (no factor) | With the factors |
|---|---|---|
| labor line | 2.75 h × 144 × 1.0 = **396.00** | 927.00 |
| missed-response credit | (2.6 × 132 + 85) × 25/100 × 1.0 = **107.05** | 465.00 |
| arrears late fee | 13702.50 × 1.5 percent × 1 = **205.54** | 107.28 |
| settlement figure | 18982.50 − 16740.00 = **2242.50** | 2761.53 |

**How each factor was reached from the customer's own records** (the words the records use):

| Factor document | The record words that led to it |
|---|---|
| Minimum Hours Standing on a Dispatched Call | the completion row's `hours_band: 'after_hours'` against `labor_hours: 2.6` |
| Prepaid Hours Standing Against the Hours of a Call | `service_block_hours_purchased` rows with `block_hours` and `expiry_date` standing on the program |
